assessments.reasoning: W3C's dated official announcement identifies the XML Core Working Group and links to the exact dated XML 1.0 Fifth Edition Recommendation. The heading and principal paragraph link the name XML to Extensible Markup Language and distinguish the fifth edition's corrections. XML identifies the markup language. W3C documents the language identity within its exact Recommendation and edition announcement. The Recommendation's element content models provide the constraint model relevant to the index scope. Interoperability with SGML and HTML does not equate their governing identities. The announcement describes XML-specific document rules.
